packets.rationale: C's 'hypothesise a mechanism from evidence (the overlay loop, an LLM fallback)'. Today only suspected_edge carries a draft (CD.3b, engine/src/suspected.rs); every other propose row has a `suggest` word and a snippet, and the model step writes the stanza. Two repairs follow from the graph alone and need no model: a route-prefix mount (gaps already names the suffix route in an unpaired_endpoint `route_prefix|edge` row's detail) and a constant pin whose value most endpoints agree on. Every row that gets no draft records why (a closed reason list), which is what turns the loop's misses into engine candidates: mealie's 45 `routes.about` owners would read `undrafted: path_member` (an object member, not a `${X}` key), three repos with the same reason are an engine packet, not three overlays.

packets.title: `glia overlay repair <repo>`: detect (health + propose), hypothesise (DECIDE.2's drafts, plus an optional external candidate a model wrote, `--candidate <file> --source model:<name>`), verify (try with leave-one-out and the health delta, keep only verdict keep with a raised mechanism and no lowered one), and with `--accept` absorb (accept's validated atomic write) plus one row per kept stanza in `.glia/repairs.jsonl`, the per-repo record; glia itself never calls a model
packets.area: C repair loop: the loop as one command + the per-repo record
packets.rationale: C, end to end. Every step exists but the person (or agent) chains them by hand (skills/glia-overlay/SKILL.md). The loop needs one call whose output is numbers, and a record that outlives the overlay file: overlay.toml holds what was absorbed, not why it was kept (the reach it raised, the gaps it closed, who proposed it, at which glia). The record is what DECIDE.6 aggregates across the cohort to promote a repair class to an engine rule. The LLM fallback is the caller, not glia: an agent with the glia-overlay skill (or any model) writes candidate TOML from propose's rows and snippets, and repair verifies and records it exactly as it does a deterministic draft, tagged with its source; off by default (no `--candidate`, no model). Nothing it writes is ever above heuristic for a model's stanza (DECIDE.3) and no fact row is created or hidden by it.

packets.implementation:
1. Detect: one `propose` (DECIDE.1 health order, DECIDE.2 drafts) over the repo(s). Nothing to repair (every mechanism OK and no draft) -> report `outcome: nothing_to_repair`, exit 0.
2. Candidate text = the drafts (unless `drafts = false`) plus `--candidate`'s stanzas (parse_candidate; a stanza without `origin` is llm by the loader's default; a `[[constraint]]` in a repair candidate is refused: repair restores structure, it states no intent, DB.9a's line). Each stanza is tagged with its source (`deterministic` for drafts, the `--source` string for the candidate's, validated `model:<name>` / `human:<name>`, 1..64 chars).
3. Verify: one `try_candidate` with leave_one_out (DECIDE.1's health delta per stanza). KEEP iff try's verdict is keep AND its health_marginal raises at least one mechanism AND lowers none AND no fact- or derived-tier edge of the base build is lost (GraphDelta per category: no category decreases except the gap categories). Otherwise review (try said review, or keep with no reach change) or dropped. A kept stanza that only closes gaps without moving reach is review: pairing must rise.
4. Absorb (only with `--accept`): `accept` (the one writer of .glia/overlay.toml, validated, atomic; reuse its pub(crate) validate / write_atomically, factored out by FC.13 if it lands first, else factored here: file overlap noted) with the kept stanzas only; then append one JSON line per kept stanza to `.glia/repairs.jsonl` (REPAIRS_FILE): `{"id":"repair:<16 hex of xxh64(stanza text)>","stanza":"<section>#<n>","class":"route_prefix|constant|edge|wrapper|<section>","source":"..","gaps":[..],"health":{"<mech>":[before,after]},"delta":{"<CATEGORY>":n},"rev":"<HEAD sha12 or worktree>","glia":"<BUILD_STAMP>"}`, sorted keys, no wall-clock time (two runs on one tree write one byte string). 3. rank_eval `--pr-intent <dir>`: load `<dir>/<label>/prs.jsonl` (+ issues.jsonl when present) with serde (code-domain's GhPr / GhIssue). A test commit is PR-MATCHED when its sha is a PR's `merge_sha` (squash / merge commit) or the LAST of a PR's `commits` (rebase merge); the PR-matched set is the subset of the existing review-shape queries (k2 / k3 / half; rank_eval's eligibility and leak-free prefix unchanged). Intent variants per query: S = the commit subject (today's ANS:review title), P = the PR title, PB = title + `\n` + body, PBI = PB + each closed issue's title + body, and the CONTROL Xperm = the PB text of ANOTHER PR-matched query of the same repo (a seeded derangement over the PR-matched queries in commit order, `--pr-seed`, default 1), so generic PR prose (templates, checklists) is measured apart from the PR's own content. Rankers rerun per variant: T1s, H9s50, LX[IDR,H9s50] (IDR over the variant's text: EB.6's route) and SELt2's online pick (the selection replay with the variant as each test commit's title, so the pick is per variant). Leak-free: a PR whose `merged_at` is after the test commit is never read for an earlier query.
4. Output: per (repo, shape, ranker) recall@10 / MRR for S / P / PB / PBI / Xperm, the paired differences with the commit-cluster bootstrap 95% CI (rank_eval's `--boot`), coverage (PR-matched queries / all queries), as markdown through `--pr-md <file>` in the `--r3md` style; bench/pr-intent/report.md is that markdown for the five repos plus the verdict.
5. PASS rule (RULE.md, before the numbers): a variant V in {P, PB, PBI} PASSES when, for SELt2's pick on the k2 shape, V - S recall@10 has CI > 0 on at least 2 repos AND on a majority of the non-thin repos, AND V - Xperm recall@10 has CI > 0 on those same repos (the gain is the PR's own text), AND V - S is not significantly negative (CI wholly < 0) on any repo or shape; the report names the best passing variant (largest mean V - S), else `FAIL`. A repo with fewer than 30 PR-matched k2 queries is `thin` and counts as neither; with fewer than 2 non-thin repos the report says the test is underpowered: FAIL, with the counts. Probe at BASE (approximate: all files, not rank_eval's candidate files): of the newest 300 eligible commits (2..=30 files) at the gate revs, PR-matched are samples 300 of 300, websocket 64 of 134, shell 58 of 300, commons-lang 29 of 300 (thin by one) and commons-io 12 of 300 (thin); so the test likely rests on 3 repos (samples, websocket, shell), and the 2-of-non-thin-majority rule then needs 2 of those 3.
6. The report line `PR intent: PASS (<variant>)` or `PR intent: FAIL (<reason>)`, aggregate numbers only.

(Written to the DEFAULT of question 1, query-time. If James rules build-time instead, the 2026-10-23 text applies with one addition: code-domain/src/snapshots.rs's module doc (:16-21, 'the build never reads it [messages.jsonl]: only query-time answers do') and CLAUDE.md's 'the build's inputs are byte-identical with or without messages' are rewritten as a declared contract break, and a byte_identical-style test pins that a build without messages.jsonl and one with it differ only by Milestone units.)
1. engine/src/goal/impact.rs (FC.8's file): `#[non_exhaustive] pub struct Milestone { pub label: String, pub files: Vec<String>, pub commits: usize, pub newest_at: i64, pub capped: usize }` and `pub(crate) fn milestones(root: &Path, merged: &MergedGraph, repo: RepoId) -> Option<(Vec<Milestone>, MilestoneStats)>`: read the history snapshot (`code_domain::snapshots::read_history(root)`) and its messages (`read_history_messages(root, &snap)`, snapshots.rs:424; None when messages.jsonl is absent -> no milestones); group commits by `HistoryMessage.br` (EB.1's merged-branch label: `pr#12`, `feat-x`, `lane@wave`; redacted when written and when read); each label's files = the union of its commits' current paths (`external::history::commit_file_sets`, history.rs:274) kept when they are MODULE files of the repo (`module_files`), capped at 300 (counted); `newest_at` = the newest commit's `at`. Milestones ordered by newest_at (oldest first), then label.
2. The diagnostic: overlap_i = |files_i ∩ files_{i-1}| / |files_i ∪ files_{i-1}| (Jaccard with its predecessor), `milestone_overlap` = the mean over i >= 1 (None with < 2 milestones). FC.8's GoalCoverage gains `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] milestone_overlap: Option<f64>` (3 dp) and `milestones: usize`; `glia goal coverage` prints `history overlap with predecessors: <o> over <m> milestones (sequential work: > 0.2; file-disjoint parallel waves: ~0)` when present.
3. `glia goal units --kind milestone` / `PyGraph.goal_units(kind="milestone")` list them as GoalUnitRow-shaped rows (ns `history`, id = the label sanitised: `#` and control chars -> `_`, <= 128 chars; state `done`; names_files = files.len(); file = `.glia/history-snapshot/commits.jsonl`, line = its newest commit's row; tier heuristic: history), computed at query time from the repo roots; no GOAL_UNIT node, no TRACES edge, no layout change. `glia goal why <file>` appends, after the TRACES paths, one `milestone` hop per milestone that touched the file (the newest 3, role `touched_in`, heuristic).
4. Marker: `[goal-milestones] repo=<l> milestones=<m> capped=<c> overlap=<o.3|none> surface=<s>` once per answer that reads them.
5. Tests (engine/tests/goal_milestones.rs, a hand-written history snapshot + messages.jsonl in a temp repo with three labelled branches, two overlapping and one disjoint): three milestones with their files, overlap = the hand-computed mean; a snapshot without messages.jsonl -> none and `goal coverage` omits the line; the built layout is byte-identical with and without messages.jsonl (the contract holds); deterministic.

1. `pub(crate) fn units_for_files(merged, files: &[(u64, String)], cap: usize) -> Vec<GoalUnitRow>` in engine/src/goal/why.rs beside FC.7's goal_units (reusing GoalUnitRow and its located rendering): the units with a TRACES edge (names_file / cites / implements, through FC.7's `traces_role`) landing on a node located in one of the files, ranked by (role order names_file < implements < cites, tier, unit qname), deduplicated by unit; never more than one hop (the why chain is `glia goal why`'s job).

The goal section is NOT part of that loop (0.5.4 correction): after the final render, compute `left = budget_tokens - used_tokens` and `goal_share = min(budget_tokens / 10, left)`; collect the packed nodes' distinct files in pack order, call units_for_files with cap = min(12, rows that fit the share), render `\n## goal context\n` + one `- <kind> <ns>/<id> "<title>" <state?> (<role>, <tier>) <file>:<line>` line per unit while the share lasts, append it to `text`, and recompute `used_tokens` / `bytes` from the final text, so `used_tokens <= budget_tokens` still holds and the node selection, rungs and order are byte-identical to the pack without units. Zero units, or a share too small for one row -> no section, no key. `Pack` gains `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] pub goal_context: Vec<PackGoalUnit>` declared right after `conventions` (`#[non_exhaustive]` PackGoalUnit; py/tests/surface/test_pack.py's PACK_KEYS pin holds because the key is skipped when empty); `empty()` (pack.rs:1271) sets it empty.
